input.question: When companies have to cut the 5% of the budget why do a lot of employees get fired? Why can't they just cut 5% of salary from everyone?
input.ground_truth: A company's budget is usually much larger than what they pay everyone. Cutting 5% can amount to far, far more money than 5% of everyone's pay. Not to mention the amount of money most large companies spend on worker's benefits. Usually an employee "costs" more to have than what they're paid. So cutting 5% of their salary will never amount to cutting them out entirely.

Now, let’s say the family finds out they don’t have enough money in their piggy bank, so they have to use 5% less money than before. That means they have a little bit less to spend.

If the family decides to just give everyone a little bit less money (like everyone gets 5% less in their pocket money), sometimes that’s possible, but sometimes it’s not enough to fix the problem. Maybe the snacks and toys they need to buy have gotten more expensive, or maybe they have to pay more for fixing the house or car.

But if the family needs to save a LOT of money really quickly, sometimes they can’t just ask everyone to take a tiny bit less. Instead, they might have to stop paying some people altogether, like letting some family members stop helping out and not get any pocket money anymore. That way, they save a bigger amount of money, but it means those people lose their jobs.

So, sometimes cutting a little bit from everyone isn’t enough, and the family has to make bigger changes, like letting some people go, to save enough money.
